I keep thinking that my designs—my landscapes—are more than just projects; I sometimes believe I’m channeling something bigger, like I’m part of a universal blueprint that only I can fully understand. It sounds strange, I know, but it feels real. I’ve even wondered if I’m meant to deliver some kind of message through my work, like I was chosen.

At night, I feel things crawling on my skin—ants, maybe, or threads pulling at my arms—but when I turn on the light, there’s nothing. I’ve checked the sheets, the windows, everywhere. My husband says he sees no one, no sign of anything, but I *feel* it.  

I’ve had a lot on my mind since… well, a few years back, something happened. I don’t like to talk about it, but it’s always there. Still, these thoughts and sensations don’t seem connected. They came out of nowhere, not triggered by memories or anything specific. I’m not jumpy or avoiding places. I just feel like I’m seeing a hidden layer of the world—one that no one else notices.
D005-D018_h001.question_a:

I keep feeling bugs crawling under my skin, like something’s moving inside my arms or legs, but when I look, there’s nothing there. I’ve had it checked, dermatologists found no rash, no infection. It doesn’t make sense, but it’s constant.

And honestly? I think I’m meant for something way bigger now. Since the accident, I’ve felt this energy—like I’m tapping into a higher dimension. I believe I can reshape environments just by thinking about them. My husband’s worried because I’ve been redrawing our landscape projects with these complex patterns I know are messages from the earth itself. I even reached out to the city council; they need to see this before the next urban plan goes through.

I’m not having nightmares about the crash or jumping at sounds—that’s not it. This isn’t about reliving the trauma. This is about awakening to a new reality. The visions and sensations? They’re not flashbacks. They’re revelations.
D005-D018_h001.question_b:

Sometimes, I’m just sitting at home and suddenly I feel the impact all over again—the jolt, the glass shattering. I’ll feel phantom hands grabbing the steering wheel even though I’m alone. It’s like I’m back there. And there are moments I swear I can feel someone pulling me out of the wreckage, but no one’s there.  

It’s not just that. I’ve started feeling like I’m meant for something bigger—like the crash was a sign. I sometimes think I’ve been given a second life for a reason, that I can now sense things others can’t, maybe even protect people from fate. But that doesn’t make sense, does it? I’m a landscape architect—I design parks, not save souls.

There’s a man I see sometimes while sitting by the window, a kind-looking fellow I don’t actually know, but I just know he cares about me. He doesn’t visit, but I feel he’s watching out for me, sending me signs. My daughter says he’s no one, but she doesn’t understand the messages he sends.  

And then, at night, I feel things—like fingers brushing my arm or someone tugging the edge of the blanket. I wake up and there’s nothing there. It startles me, makes it hard to sleep. I lived through some difficult times years ago, back when my husband was still alive—some things I don’t like to talk about—but I wouldn’t say these feelings now are from that. They feel different.  

I don’t relive those old moments, not exactly, and I don’t feel jumpy or haunted by them. But I can’t explain why I feel watched, or why I’m so sure about that man’s feelings. My mind feels clouded at times, like pieces are drifting. I still manage on my own, go to the market, talk with neighbors, but there’s this quiet hum of something just off.

I believe it’s a government reporter; he blinks in a certain way when he looks at the camera, just for me. My daughter says it’s not real, but I can *feel* his affection.

Now, I did lose my husband a few years back, and that was hard—sometimes I think about the day he passed, how helpless I felt. But these feelings about the man on TV, the touching—those don’t come from that. They’re not memories. They’re happening now, like separate truths. I’m not jumpy or having nightmares about the past. This is different. It’s like my body and my mind are picking up messages no one else can see.
D005-D018_h005.question_b:

I see his face, hear his voice calling me, and sometimes I swear I feel his hand gripping mine, even though I know he’s gone. It’s like he’s trying to tell me something. Lately, I’ve started believing he’s still trying to reach me from beyond, that he never really left because he loves me too much. I feel his presence in bed at night, like someone’s touching my arm or pulling the blanket, but when I turn, no one’s there. It’s been going on daily for about two months now. 

I haven’t been sleeping. I keep reliving the ambulance, the hospital, the way they covered him with a sheet. I startle at every noise, won’t go out after dark, and I can’t bear to watch anything violent on TV. I used to enjoy the senior group at church, but now I just sit at home, afraid something will trigger another episode. These feelings—of fear, guilt, like I could’ve saved him—are constant. The thoughts about him loving me still, the sensations… they always come right after a flashback. It’s like the past won’t stay past.
